purpose: From-scratch rerun that changes exactly two variables versus the current baseline: (1) EMA weights are used for validation and checkpoint selection, (2) the BEV head trains at 0.5x the base learning rate. Network, loss weights, data, batch and clip are unchanged.

hypothesis.ema: smoothing the weights should reduce epoch-to-epoch swings of val/paper_loss and stop the late-epoch drift
hypothesis.bev_lr: halving the BEV head step should stop its monotonic degradation (currently +8-9% over 20 epochs) because the head only receives 0.55% of the gradient norm and keeps overshooting
hypothesis.combined: BEV and total validation loss should improve without hurting agent/trajectory branches

baseline_reference.note: Same formula and same data as this run, so val/paper_loss is directly comparable
baseline_reference.known_issue: train/loss fell 73.9% while val/paper_loss rose 3.8%; cosine annealing was ruled out as the cause

2_bev_head_lr.note: image_encoder keeps its existing official 0.5x; the BEV head is the only new multiplier

unchanged_from_baseline: official V1 model architecture and loss weights (12/10/8/20/10/1/14) untouched
dataset, split, 8:1:1 seed-0 Route split, tail policy untouched
batch 16 x accumulate 4 = effective 64, clip 1000, num_workers 8 untouched
base learning_rate 3e-4 with WarmupCosLR 50 epochs / warmup 3 / min_lr 1e-6
BF16 convolution engineering policy; loss and eval stay FP32
full 17,191-row validation every epoch; monitor val/paper_loss

validation.objective: paper-v1: forward_train branch, frozen dropout, seed=epoch*100003+batch_idx
validation.weights: EMA shadow (decay 0.999, warmed up over first 100 steps)
validation.extra_cost: one extra weight copy per validation, plus one 2-step diffusion forward per batch

test.usage: not loaded during training, checkpoint selection or tuning

checkpoint_semantics.best-*.ckpt / last.ckpt: raw weights, consistent with the saved optimizer state; the monitored score was produced by the EMA weights
checkpoint_semantics.ema-*.ckpt: smoothed weights only (schema status-ema-weights-v1); use these for evaluation or deployment
checkpoint_semantics.resume: always from last.ckpt or pause-*.ckpt (raw weights); the EMA shadow is restored from callback state

ema_effect: epoch-to-epoch standard deviation of val/paper_loss over a 5-epoch window is lower than the baseline window (76.49, 76.77, 77.06, 75.89, 77.17 -> sigma 0.54)
no late-epoch monotonic rise comparable to ep29-31 (+2.2 over three epochs)
bev_effect: val/paper_bev_semantic_loss stays at or below the ep28 value 6.00 instead of climbing past 6.20
val/paper_bev_semantic_loss does not exceed 1.3x its best-so-far value
no_collateral_damage: val/paper_trajectory_loss does not exceed the baseline best 65.75 by more than 3%
overall: val/paper_loss reaches a new minimum below 75.89
train/val gap does not widen beyond the current 5.1x

stop_or_investigate_if: val/paper_loss rises for three consecutive epochs
agent or trajectory branch loss exceeds 1.5x its best-so-far value
guardrails: exactly two variables changed: EMA on, BEV head lr_mult 0.5; everything else identical to the baseline
official repository stays byte-identical (only the pre-existing scheduler verbose patch)
loss weights untouched, so val/paper_loss stays comparable with ep25-31
EMA weights are used for validation; checkpoints keep raw weights so resume stays consistent
Test split frozen and never loaded
